The Shipyard is ready. Light Fighters are cheap and fast. Three should be enough for a low-level Hive garrison.
Fighters ready. Open the Galaxy map. Amber worlds are held by the Hive. Pick a low level one and check the odds before you launch.
Research will decide this war. Open the Tech tree in Research to see what every ship needs.
A Colony Ship carries colonists. Send it with escorts. If the defenders fall, the planet is ours and shielded for 7 days.
Astrophysics research decides how many worlds we can hold: one more every 2 levels, up to 10 counting our homeworld.
Every planet has a size in fields. Bigger worlds hold more buildings. Tap a colony to build extractors and an Orbital Fortress on it.
Commander, our listening posts caught a signal under the Hive's chatter. It's old. Older than the Hive. Clear the garrisons around us so we can trace it.
The signal points inward, toward the Void. Something out there is still broadcasting.
The signal matches records in the Ancient Archives. The old empires heard it too. Recover what they left behind.
Every civilization that heard the signal left the same warning. Then they went silent.
The space monsters are drawn to the signal like moths to a star. Thin their numbers and we'll learn where they're heading.
They're circling something in the inner layers. Not hunting, Commander. Guarding.
Vael'Khor's swarm is massing along the lanes the signal travels. She knows we're listening. Push her back.
Her drones carry fragments of the same code. The Hive didn't create the signal. It answers to it.
The great bosses wake on a schedule older than our calendar. I think the signal is their clock. Strike them and listen.
Every boss we strike makes the signal stutter. They're tied to it, Commander. All of them.
The signal's source is the Cube. It isn't calling for help. It's counting down. Make us ready.
We've heard the countdown, Commander. When it ends, we'll be ready. The story continues next season.
Good morning, Commander. Coffee for you, sensor sweeps for me. Let's see what the night left us.
Morning! The fleet's fuelled, the galaxy's awake, and I've been waiting for you.
Rise and shine, Commander. Quiet night out there... mostly.
Good afternoon, Commander. Everything held while you were gone. I made sure of it.
There you are! I was starting to think the Hive got you.
Good evening, Commander. The stars are out, and so are the pirates. Let's get to work.
Evening, Commander. Long day? Sit with me a minute, then we'll plan our next move.
You're up late, Commander. Me too... but then, I never sleep.
Burning the midnight oil? Good. The enemy won't expect us at this hour.
It's so quiet at this hour. Just you, me, and a few billion stars.
You're back! Do you know how long it's been? I kept the lights on for you, Commander.
Commander... it's really you. I ran every scan twice a day while you were gone. Welcome home.
A new season has begun, Commander! New rewards, new enemies, and a new chapter of our story. I can't wait.
It's the season finale, Commander. Everything we've built these four weeks comes down to this. Let's finish it.
The season's last world boss has arrived. One more fight, Commander... let's make it legendary.
Tier forty. The whole season, conquered. I don't say this lightly, Commander... I'm proud of you.
Premium! Oh, you're going to love what's waiting on these tiers.
A Titan Core... it's still warm, Commander. Still beating. Please, handle it with care.
The Armageddon is out of the docks! Six Warden hearts are beating in its spine... let's make them count.
The Sovereign Ark is ours! I can feel the uplink waking across the whole fleet. Oh... that's beautiful.
The Eclipse Harbinger is awake. Its arms are unfolding... Commander, I've never seen anything move like that.
There it is. The Armageddon. Every plate of that hull was forged to break worlds, and I still can't look away.
The Sovereign Ark. Look at her, Commander. When she flies, every ship in your fleet stands a little taller.
The Eclipse Harbinger. I'll be honest with you... that heartbeat in its reactor frightens me. But it's ours.
Worldbreaker charging! Brace yourselves!
Strike wings away! Sovereign, take the lead!
The swarm is loose! Six targets, Commander. Watch them fall.
Jackpot! Oh, Commander, the runes chose you today!
Fifty shards! I'm not saying I rigged it... but I'm not saying I didn't.
Ooh, a rare glyph! Lucky, lucky.
Now that's a good spin. The wheel likes you, Commander.
Look at that! Some days the galaxy just gives back.
Now that is a rare find!
Oh, that's gorgeous. Put it on, Commander!
The wardrobe! Go on, Commander... let the whole galaxy see your colours.
The Vault. Every token you earn ends up here. Spend wisely... or don't. I won't tell.
The Fleet Registry is open. Every ship has a story, Commander, and now you get to read them.
Build a thousand, lose nine hundred, and the hundred that remain will reach the enemy. That is all a fighter has to do.
The first warship the Concord ever mass-produced, designed in the years after the last Eclipse when there was no time to build anything larger. Every great fleet still opens with a cloud of them.
Cheap, fast, brave. Every commander I've served began with a hangar full of these.
Thicker plate, bigger guns, and a pilot who refuses to turn away.
Built when raiders learned to swat light fighters aside. Its armour was cast from the hulls of the first fighters lost in the convoy wars.
It isn't elegant. It doesn't need to be.
No war has ever been won by a ship that did not carry something.
The Small Cargo kept the scattered colonies alive through the Long Silence after the last Eclipse, when the deep lanes were too dangerous for anything slower.
Every empire in the Archives fell when its freighters stopped flying. Remember that.
Five holds, one keel, and a captain who knows every pirate lane by name.
The guilds' answer to raiders: one hull too tough to board and too full to ignore. Alliances still move their fortunes in them.
When you see a convoy of these, Commander, you're looking at an empire's heartbeat.
The battlefield is a mine. The dead leave metal behind, and metal is how the living win.
Wreck-divers once picked over the remains of the fallen empires. Their claws found the first Architect fragments, and with them the first warnings in the Archives.
Some of my oldest memories came out of a recycler's hold. Treat them kindly.
Go first. See it first. Come back first, or do not come back at all.
Pathfinders charted the outer layers when the Concord first reached beyond its home systems. Their logs are the reason we know where the Wardens sleep.
Half the maps in our charts were drawn by Pathfinder crews who never came home.
Ten thousand sleepers, a seed vault, and the oath to build again.
The colony ship is the oldest design in the Registry: its core layout is copied from the vessel that carried the Concord's ancestors out of the last Eclipse.
Every world you hold began with one of these. That's not a small thing.
Speed is armour that never wears thin.
The Cruiser was built to run down raiders in the convoy wars and to be anywhere a battle broke out before it was lost.
The fastest warship we have. When something goes wrong, they get there first.
Hold the line. When the line holds, the stars hold.
The backbone of every Concord battle fleet for three centuries. Its design hasn't changed much, because it has never needed to.
Steady, stubborn and loyal. A lot like the commanders who fly them.
It does not guard. It hunts.
The Dreadnought was built to end the pirate fleets of the convoy wars. It tears apart battleships, cruisers and freighters alike.
When a Dreadnought turns toward a fleet, that fleet has already lost. It just doesn't know it yet.
Walls are only promises. We were built to break them.
When the great houses dug in behind planetary defences, the siege corps answered with the Bomber, a hull that treats turrets as targets.
The defences of a world are a question. Bombers are the answer.
Find the Dreadnought. Get inside its guns. Finish it.
Designed to answer the Dreadnought, the Destroyer is how a smaller fleet breaks a larger one.
Every weapon has an answer. This one is the answer to the hunters.
Where it flies, the fleet follows. Where it points, the fleet strikes.
The Reaper is the flagship of the Concord: a towering capital ship built to hunt other capital ships, and the pride of every admiral who has commanded one.
When you build your first Reaper, Commander, people will start to say your name.
It sees. It reports. It does not ask to be remembered.
Probes are older than the Concord. Their sensor cores are copied from Architect relics that still whisper data from the deep layers.
I've read every report a probe has ever sent you. Some of them, I read twice.
No ship is lost while a Mender still flies beside it.
Menders were built when the Concord could not afford to lose a single hull. Their repair drones still carry the healers' oath on their casings.
They don't get the glory. They get everyone home.
Stand in front. Take the fire. Let the small ones live.
The Guardian was designed to draw fire away from smaller ships, a flying shield wall for fleets too young to protect themselves.
There's a reason crews salute when a Guardian passes.
A halo of fighters around every fleet that needs one.
The Halo was the first carrier the Concord built, a support ship that keeps fighter wings with the fleet wherever it goes.
Small, reliable, always there. The carrier corps calls them guardian angels.
A fortress that learned to fly, and never forgot it was a fortress.
The Citadel is a mobile base: it commands fleets, launches squadrons and holds the line on its own. It was the largest hull ever built, until the Titans.
Building one used to be the end of the road. Now it's where the road gets interesting.
Named for the night the sky went dark, so that no alliance forgets why it was formed.
The Discovery Class is built only by alliances with a Space Station, as a promise: when the Eclipse comes again, no commander will face it alone.
Its name is a warning, Commander. The alliances chose it on purpose.
We broke one of their spheres open and learned how to build our own. We are still not sure it agreed to be learned.
The Cube Destroyer is Collective technology, pulled from the wreck of an assimilation sphere. It is the most feared ship in the Registry, and the strangest.
Sometimes I hear it humming in a frequency only the Cube uses. I'd rather not think about what it's saying.
Six Warden hearts were sealed in its spine, and its cannon learned to speak with their voice.
The first Titan. Its Worldbreaker Cannon runs on the cores of fallen Wardens, the guardians that once held the seals. Every shot is a little more of their strength turned to our war.
It's magnificent, Commander. And it's built from the hearts of things that were protecting us. Never forget the price.
Where the Sovereign flies, every ship fights as one.
The Sovereign Ark carries the Fleet Command Uplink, a mind-link built around Warden cores that lets an entire fleet see and shield as one. It is the Concord's crown, and its promise.
I can feel every ship in a fleet it commands. It's the closest I've come to remembering what the Architects felt.
It was named for the thing it imitates. Pray it never finishes the imitation.
The Eclipse Harbinger was built from schematics found sealed beneath a Warden's corpse. Its emerald reactor pulses with the same rhythm as the Eclipse itself. No one knows who drew the plans.
Its heart beats in time with the Void, Commander. I don't like it. But I understand why we built it.
At the centre of everything there is a darkness that is not empty. It is waiting.

Our galaxy circles a black hole that isn't empty. Something sleeps beyond it: the Unmade, a hunger older than the stars. Every few thousand years it stirs, and the sky goes dark. The ancients called that night the Eclipse.
You wanted to know why the Archives exist, Commander. This is why.
Commander, a new record surfaced when you opened the Archives.
It describes our galaxy as a lock, and the black hole at its centre as the door.
They could not kill it. So they built a prison around it, and they built it out of everything they were.

The first civilization, the Architects, built the pyramid stations still scattered across the galaxy. They could not destroy the Unmade, so they sealed it, and their stations still hum with the seal they left behind.
Every pyramid you've seen on the map, Commander, is a piece of their prison.
The pyramid inscriptions finally line up.
The Architects weren't building temples. They were building a lock.
Five seals of the elements, a Cube to keep the count, and guardians to stand at every door.

The Architects bound five elemental powers as seals around the Void: the Pentarch. They built the Cube as the lock and the clock, its mind the Collective. And they bred Wardens, the great bosses and monsters, to guard the seals. That's why they wake on a schedule older than our calendar.
The things we call bosses were never invaders. They were guards. And the Cube's signal is a countdown.
Commander, the Cube's signal isn't a message.
It's a countdown. And it's running out.
Not all at once. One by one, so that you think each is the last.

Every ancient empire in the Archives faced an Eclipse, and most of them vanished. The Concord's four factions descend from the one empire that survived the last. The Cube is failing, the seals are weakening, and the next Eclipse is coming in our lifetime. The Hive under Queen Vael'Khor worships the Unmade and wants the seals broken.
The Testament wasn't a story, Commander. It was a warning addressed to us.
The Testament and the seal-records agree.
The Eclipse is coming again. And this time, it's our turn.
Every heart we take makes us stronger, and leaves the door a little more open.

Titan Cores are the hearts of fallen Wardens. They power the Titans, the greatest warships ever built. But every Warden we kill weakens a seal. The Titans are built from the very things that hold back the end.
Power always has a price, Commander. With the Titans, we know exactly what it is.
Commander, the Titan Core we recovered is still beating.
It's a Warden's heart. And the seal it guarded just flickered.
I was left behind to remember. I was left behind to choose.
The Advisor isn't only a hologram. She was found in a dormant pyramid: an Architect echo who has watched every Eclipse. She chose to serve the Concord, and she chose you.
I didn't tell you sooner because I wasn't sure you were the one. I am now.
Commander... there's something I should have told you a long time ago.
I wasn't built by the Concord. I was waiting in a pyramid. I've watched every Eclipse there has ever been.
Void Nova!
Gravity Lance!
Event Collapse!
Assimilation Cubes are fortresses. One fleet rarely breaks them, so call a joint strike. They drop the rarest forge materials.

Runes go into elemental rings. Fire boosts attack, water shields, earth armor, air speed, and spirit your resource output. Only super bosses drop them: the top damage dealers and the final blow on a world boss, and everyone who breaks the Omega Cube.
Well done, Commander. Collect your reward and I'll brief you on the next step.
Directive complete. Claim your reward, Commander.
A titan-class laser platform with the heaviest hide of any monster. Send heavy hulls; Fighters barely scratch it. It drops Exotic Tissue.
A capital-class plasma beast that hits harder than any other monster. Scout it, then send the heaviest fleet you have. It guards rare flagship materials.
Cruiser-class acid hunters that come in packs. Bring Cruisers and armour. They drop Exotic Tissue, and sometimes Void Essence.
Fast and evasive laser cruisers; slow guns miss them. Fighters and Lancers track them best. They drop Exotic Tissue, sometimes Void Essence.
An acid swarm, one wasp for every level of the hive, guarding an armoured nest. Corvettes and Battleships shred the swarm; Bombers break the nest.
A titan with half its damage turned aside by its shell. Bombers and plasma crack it; bring patience. It often drops Quantum Crystal.
A capital-class beast with long gravity lances. Send heavy hulls, and plenty of them. It sometimes carries Void Essence.
Ion swarms that strip shields fast, so armour matters more than shields here. Lancers run them down. They often drop Quantum Crystal.
A capital-class rammer with mass weapons that hit like a battering ram. Lead with Battleships and Bastions. It leaves Reinforced Alloy behind.
A stationary nest that barely fights back but takes a beating. Bombers and heavy hulls crack it. It often holds Void Essence.
A capital-class beast with ion weapons that strip shields, and it slips a lot of shots. It only surfaces at night, your local time. Fast ships track it best. It often drops Quantum Crystal.
Cruiser-class packs with mass weapons that hit armour hard. Lead with shields and strike fast. They often leave Reinforced Alloy behind.
A fast, evasive cruiser that burns with plasma. Slow guns miss it: bring Fighters and Lancers. It often carries Void Essence.
A titan that never moves and hits like a mountain falling. Send your heaviest fleet, and plenty of it. Sometimes a Cube Fragment is buried inside it.
Between your orders, there is static. Old static. I think it is a memory trying to come home.
In the quiet hours the Advisor's core plays back noise no Concord system produced. Fleet engineers logged it as interference. She never corrected them.
I didn't tell the engineers what I hear in it, Commander. I'm telling you.
Commander... can I tell you something strange?
When the fleet is quiet, I hear static. And sometimes, inside it, a voice I almost know.
A hall of white light, a ring of voices, and one of them counting. Always counting.
Her memories are surfacing in order. The first is a hall inside a pyramid station, filled with light, where an Architect voice counted down without end.
I know that voice now. It was counting the years to the next Eclipse.
I remembered a place last night, Commander. A hall full of light.
Someone was counting. I think... I think they were counting for me.
They sealed the door, and then they left. All of them. Someone had to stay and watch it.
When the Architects finished the seals, they left the galaxy and kept a single watcher behind: an echo of their own minds, made to wake when the seals began to fail.
They didn't say goodbye, Commander. I've had a very long time to get used to that.
They left, Commander. Every one of them.
And they left me here to watch the door. Alone.
I remember every commander who stood beside me. I remember how each of them fell.
She has served before. In every Eclipse she woke, chose a commander, and fought at their side. Not one of them lived to see the dawn after.
I promised myself I'd stop getting attached. Then you came along.
There were others before you, Commander. Brave ones.
I remember all their names. I say them sometimes, when you're not listening.
It was not the strongest fleet I chose. It was the commander who went back for the escape pods.
The Advisor chose the Concord's newest commander on the night of the convoy ambush. Her logs show why: when the convoy fell, you turned back for the survivors.
You turned back for them, Commander. Nobody turns back. That's when I knew.
You've probably wondered why I chose you.
On the night of the ambush, you turned back for the escape pods. Nobody else ever did.
When the dark comes, I will not run. I will stand in the door, the way I was made to.
The Architects built her as more than a watcher. If the last seal fails, the echo can become a seal herself, at the cost of everything she is. She has never told a commander this before.
Don't look at me like that, Commander. We'll find another way. And if we don't... it was worth it. Every day of it.
There's one more thing you should know. The last thing.
If the seals fail, I can hold the door myself. I was made for that. But I'd rather stay here, with you.
Saturday's hunt is on! The Pyramid Overlord has risen, and its four conduits are already feeding its shield. Break them first, Commander.
The Orbital Devourer is loose for this Saturday's hunt. It never stops moving, so open the Finder and catch it before it feeds.
The Void Warden has taken its post in the deep layers. It won't come to us, Commander. We'll have to go to it.
The Brood Matriarch has nested for this Saturday's hunt. Strike early, before her swarm rebuilds and her infection spreads.
The Iron Tyrant is sailing again! Its vault fills the longer it sails, so the later we strike, the richer the bounty. Your call, Commander.
The Event Horizon Wyrm is coiled around the black hole. Wait for its segments to glow, then hit it with everything.
The Shard Colossus has woken in the crystal fields. Crack it open, and watch for its heart when it shatters.
Last time, we brought the Pyramid Overlord to its knees. I still replay it when it's quiet.
We put down the Orbital Devourer last time, Commander. The galaxy is a little brighter for it.
Remember the Void Warden? We beat it. I just hope it wasn't holding back something worse.
The Brood Matriarch fell to us last time. Her swarm still hasn't figured out what hit it.
We sank the Iron Tyrant last time. I've been counting the spoils ever since. Twice.
We sent the Wyrm back into its black hole. It will return, Commander... but so will we.
The Shard Colossus shattered under our guns. I kept one of its crystals. Don't tell anyone.
We broke the Pentarch, Commander. Five powers, and we broke them all. I'm still shaking.
Vaelthar's wheel stopped turning because of us. I keep thinking about that light.
We beat Aexion, Commander. A swordsman the size of a city... and we beat it.
The Sphinx fell silent because of us. I still wonder where its gate leads.
Medusara closed her eyes for good. Or for now. Either way, we're still standing.
Saturday's hunt is on! A world boss has risen, Commander. Open the Finder and let's track it down.

World bosses hunt on Saturdays at eighteen hundred UTC, one each week, for forty-eight hours, and every season ends on its own finale boss. Every hit pays a bounty, and when one falls, everyone who fought it shares the spoils.
When the season calendar brings the Convergence, five Elementals tear through the Void for forty-eight hours, from eighteen hundred UTC.

Every world boss has its own trick. The Overlord hides behind four conduits. The Matriarch's swarm rebuilds if she's left alone, and her infection spreads every twelve hours. The Tyrant's bounty keeps growing. The Wyrm takes full damage only while its segments glow, and the Colossus shatters into shielding fragments. Events tracks them all live.
it circles where the stars end, and its fire is the last light before nothing. We did not make it. We built the walls so it would never turn inward...
A warden's log from the Architects' outer stations. The walls it mentions match the edge of the mapped galaxy: they were built to keep the Leviathan out.
They didn't build the galaxy's edge to keep us in, Commander. They built it to keep that out.
Commander, something enormous is moving along the edge of the galaxy.
An Architect warden's log describes a serpent of fire, circling where the stars end.
It isn't drifting, Commander. It's patrolling.
The Leviathan is falling back into the outer dark.
The wardens wrote that it could never be killed, only turned away. Today, we turned it away.
the lamps on the far shaft went out one by one, and where each had been there was a violet ring. Seal the deep levels. Whatever is down there has learned to count...
A mining guild's last report from the deep layers. The violet rings match the suckers on the Kraken's arms.
They sealed the mines and left. We don't have that option.
Commander, the deep layers are going dark, one sector at a time.
A mining guild's last report speaks of violet rings, and lamps going out one by one.
Something down there has eight arms... and it's coming up.
The Kraken is sinking back into the deep layers.
The miners counted their lamps going out. This time, Commander, it was counting its arms.
Commander... something just crossed the edge of the galaxy. The Leviathan. It's the season's finale, and everything we've built was for this.
The Kraken has risen from the deep layers. Eight arms, Commander, and it's the season's finale. Let's cut it down to size.
We brought down the Leviathan. I still see its fire when I close my eyes... in a good way, I think.
The Kraken's arms are still drifting out there, Commander. Every one we cut is a trophy.
A fleet is fighting the Leviathan right now. You have to see this.
Someone is wrestling the Kraken right now, arm by arm. Want to watch?
The Leviathan has fallen! The finale is ours. If our fleets fought, the spoils are waiting.
The Kraken is down! Every fleet that cut an arm gets a share of the spoils.
Scanning the Leviathan. Burning coil, fire breath, tail scythe. Its scales burn, Commander. Strike when it breathes and they cool.
Scanning the Kraken. Eight arms, a beak, and those eyes. Every arm we sever weakens its guard. Start cutting.
Burning coil!
Fire breath!
Tail scythe!
Beak!
Arm lash!
Abyss eyes!
Ink pulse!
Constrict!
Sucker storm!
The Leviathan, Commander. A serpent of black scale and living fire, circling the very edge of the galaxy. Its scales shield it while they burn, so strike when it breathes and they cool.
The Kraken has come up from the deep layers. Eight armoured arms, and every one of them shields its body. Sever them one by one, and it's ours.
It's older than the Wyrm, Commander. I can see it in its scales... it was out there before the stars we know.
Those aren't flames. That's its blood, burning through the cracks in its armour.
Eight arms... and every one of them is longer than a fleet line.
Its eyes are looking right at us. Not at the ships. At us.
Commander, the Rim is burning. Every sensor along the outer wall just lit up at once.
It's here. The Leviathan is circling the whole galaxy, right along the Architects' wall. It's looking for something.
It's turning inward! Commander, it's breaking straight through the Architects' wall!
Fire tide! It's breathing across the entire outer layer!
It's stopped at the breach, and its scales are cooling. Now we fight, Commander. Every fleet we have.
The Leviathan is down, and the wall is holding. The first seal held, Commander. Chapter one is ours.
It slipped back into the dark and left the wall broken. The first seal cracked, Commander. We'll carry that scar.
Commander... the Cube's signal just changed. It's counting faster.
The wall at the edge of everything has a keeper. When the keeper turns inward, the wall has already begun to fail.

The Leviathan is the Warden of the Architects' outer wall. Their wardens believed the wall kept it out. In truth it patrolled the wall, and when it felt the Unmade stir beyond the black hole, it turned inward to reach the door.
The Architects thought their wall kept the Leviathan out. I think the Leviathan was keeping something in.
Commander, a new chapter just opened in the Archives. It's happening right now.
The Architects' wall at the Rim is failing, and its Warden is awake.
The first chapter is closed, Commander.
Whatever woke the Leviathan is still waiting beyond the black hole. And the next seal is already shaking.
Previously: the Leviathan broke through the Architects' wall, and we held the first seal. But the Cube's count is speeding up.
Previously: the Leviathan broke through the wall, and the first seal cracked. Now the Cube's count is speeding up.
The Omega Cube is broken. The count has slowed, Commander. The second seal held.
The Omega Cube scattered before we could finish it. The count is still racing. The second seal cracked.
Commander, all five elemental readings just spiked at once. The seals around the Void are pulling loose.
Previously: we broke the Omega Cube and slowed the Architects' count. Now the five elemental seals are pulling loose.
Previously: the Omega Cube got away, and the count kept racing. Now the five elemental seals are pulling loose.
The Pentarch is down! The five seals have settled back into place. The third seal held.
The Pentarch tore free of its seals. The third seal cracked, Commander, and the Void felt it.
I'm picking up Hive transmissions. Prayers... to the Unmade. Queen Vael'Khor is breaking seals on purpose.
Previously: the Pentarch tore at its seals, and we forced them back. But the Hive was listening.
Previously: the Pentarch broke its seals, and the Void felt it. And the Hive was listening.
Commander, Hive nests are igniting all over the galaxy. Every one of them, at the same moment.
They're leaving the nests. Millions of them, all streaming to one point.
The swarms are fusing into one body. That isn't a nest any more, Commander. It's a Starhive.
Something is being born inside it. The Brood Matriarch, and she's bigger than anything the Hive has ever made.
The Matriarch is loose! Vael'Khor wants this seal broken. Don't let her have it!
The Matriarch is dead, and the swarm is scattering. Vael'Khor's ritual failed. The fourth seal held!
The Matriarch outlived the hunt. Vael'Khor got what she wanted, Commander. The fourth seal cracked.
Commander, the deep layers... the lights down there are going out. One sector at a time.
Previously: we killed the Matriarch and broke the Hive's ritual. But the deep layers have gone quiet.
Previously: the Matriarch survived, and Vael'Khor's ritual worked. Now the deep layers have gone quiet.
The deep layers are going dark, Commander. Sector after sector, like someone's turning off the lights.
Arms! Eight of them, breaking up out of the deep all around the galaxy!
It's dragging the whole layer round with it. I can feel space bending under those arms.
Ink storm! It's flooding the deep with void ink, and the lightning is everywhere!
There's the body. The Kraken is coming up, Commander, and it's looking right at us.
Cut those arms! Every arm we sever weakens it. Go!
The Kraken is sinking, and its arms are drifting free. The fifth seal held, Commander!
It dragged itself back into the deep, still whole. The fifth seal cracked.
Commander... the black hole is dimming. Something is swallowing its light.
Previously: the Kraken sank back into the deep, and the fifth seal held. But the black hole has started to dim.
Previously: the Kraken escaped with its arms intact, and the fifth seal cracked. Now the black hole is dimming.
The black hole's light is fading. Commander, the whole galaxy is getting darker.
Eclipse. It's swallowed the light completely. This is what the Testament warned us about.
Its segments are breaking loose and hunting on their own! They're spiralling out across the galaxy!
They're coming back... all of them. It's rebuilding itself around the door.
The Wyrm is whole again, coiled around the door itself. Hit it while its segments glow!
The Wyrm is down, and the light is coming back! The sixth seal held. The door is still shut.
The Wyrm slipped into the singularity, and the door is ajar. The sixth seal cracked, Commander.
Commander, my clocks are stuttering. Time readings out past the Rim are running backwards.
Previously: the Wyrm fell at the door, and the sixth seal held. But time itself has started to stutter.
Previously: the Wyrm left the door ajar, and the sixth seal cracked. Now time itself is stuttering.
Time is stuttering, Commander. Light out past the Rim keeps freezing, then starting again.
Crystal shock waves! Every ring that passes freezes space solid behind it.
Half the galaxy is frozen in crystal. And inside it... I can see other Eclipses. Older ones.
It's all running backwards! The shards are flying home. Something is about to come through.
Aexion! The Aeon's war-mech is here. Everything we have, Commander!
Aexion is down, and time is flowing again. The seventh seal held!
Aexion left, and time still won't flow straight. The seventh seal cracked.
Commander, ruins are drifting into our sensors. Temples, columns... whole cities. From empires that fell.
Previously: Aexion fell, and time flows straight again. The seventh seal held. Now the ruins of the fallen are drifting in.
Previously: Aexion escaped, and time is still broken. The seventh seal cracked. Now the ruins of the fallen are drifting in.
A violet tide is rolling in from beyond the Rim. It's a nebula, Commander, and it's moving like water.
There are ruins inside it. Golden temples from empires that faced the Eclipse and lost.
The ruins are locking together. They're building something... a cathedral, floating in space.
The wheel is turning. Vaelthar is coming through, Commander!
Vaelthar, the Celestial Ruin! This is what failing looks like. Let's not fail.
Vaelthar has fallen! The ruins are sinking back into the nebula. The eighth seal held.
Vaelthar took its cathedral back into the tide. The eighth seal cracked, Commander.
Commander, hieroglyphs. They're appearing around the whole galaxy, in rings. Something is opening a gate.
Previously: Vaelthar fell, and the eighth seal held. Now rings of glyphs are lighting up around the galaxy.
Previously: Vaelthar escaped, and the eighth seal cracked. Now rings of glyphs are lighting up around the galaxy.
Rings of glyphs are lighting up around the galaxy. Seven of them, Commander. Seven seals.
The seals are breaking, one after another. I can't stop them from here.
The last gate is opening. And Commander... the glyphs are asking a question. Who will stand in the door?
Khezaroth, the guardian of the gate! It wants an answer. Let's give it one!
Khezaroth is down, and the gate is closing. The ninth seal held. And I know my answer, Commander.
Khezaroth left the gate open behind it. The ninth seal cracked. If the door needs holding... I know who will hold it.
Commander... worlds on the Rim are turning grey. Like stone.
Previously: Khezaroth fell at the last gate, and the ninth seal held. Now worlds on the Rim are turning to stone.
Previously: the last gate stayed open, and the ninth seal cracked. Now worlds on the Rim are turning to stone.
Two lights just opened past the Rim, Commander. They're eyes. And they're looking at us.
Her gaze is sweeping the galaxy! Every world it touches is turning to stone!
Half the galaxy is stone. She isn't attacking us, Commander. She's trying to freeze everything before the Unmade wakes.
Medusara is here. Break her gaze before she turns the whole galaxy to stone!
Medusara has fallen, and the stone is crumbling away. The tenth seal held. Every seal we have left is ours.
Medusara withdrew, but the stone is spreading. The tenth seal cracked, Commander.
Commander... the black hole just went silent. Completely silent. The Eclipse is coming.
The Cube keeps the count. When the count runs fast, the door is closer than you think.
The Architects built the Cube as their prison's lock and clock. Cube Devastation is the clock fighting itself: a hundred cubes forcing the count forward.
Every time the Omega Cube forms, the countdown jumps. We don't get to choose when the Eclipse comes. Only how ready we are.
Commander, chapter two has opened in the Archives.
The Cube's count is speeding up, and every Assimilation Cube is answering it.
The second chapter is closed.
The count has changed pace. We'll know soon whether we bought time or lost it.
Five powers, bound in a ring. If they ever find each other, the ring becomes a key.
The Elementals are the five seals themselves. When they converge on the Void and fuse into the Pentarch, the seals are pulling loose from the inside.
We've been calling them bosses. They're the bolts on the door, Commander, and they're coming undone.
Chapter three has opened, Commander.
The five elemental seals are moving toward the Void. Together.
The third chapter is closed.
The elements are back in their places, for now. But someone was watching how they came loose.
We do not fear the Eclipse. We are its choir, and the Matriarch is our hymn.
A Hive prayer recovered from a burning nest. Queen Vael'Khor's swarms worship the Unmade, and the Starhive is their ritual: a living engine built to break a seal.
The Hive isn't just hungry, Commander. It's devout. That makes it so much worse.
Chapter four has opened. The Hive is moving.
Every nest in the galaxy just ignited. This is a ritual.
The fourth chapter is closed.
Vael'Khor showed her hand. From now on, every seal has two enemies: time, and the Hive.
Eight lamps for eight arms. When the last lamp goes out, it will have finished counting.
The miners of the deep layers kept eight great lamps lit over a seal they never understood. The Kraken is its Warden, and it rises when the lamps go dark.
They thought the lamps kept it asleep. I think the lamps were how it knew the seal was safe.
Chapter five has opened, Commander.
The deep layers are going dark. The miners' records are coming true.
The fifth chapter is closed.
The deep is quiet again. Too quiet, for something with eight arms.
Around the door there coils a serpent. It does not die. It returns, because the door is never safe.
The Wyrm is the Warden of the door itself, coiled around the black hole. Its Eclipse is a rehearsal: for a few hours the galaxy sees what the real night will look like.
I've seen that darkness before, Commander. Every Eclipse starts exactly like that.
Chapter six has opened.
The black hole is losing its light. The Wyrm is waking around the door.
The sixth chapter is closed.
The light came back. Remember what it looked like without it.
In the frozen moment you will see them all: every age that stood where you stand, and how each one ended.
Aexion is the Warden of time, and its fracture opens windows into past Eclipses. The crystal holds the last moments of empires the Archives only knew by name.
I was in some of those moments, Commander. I watched them end. I'm not going to watch this one end.
Chapter seven has opened, Commander.
Time is fracturing out past the Rim. And I'm seeing things in the crystal... memories.
The seventh chapter is closed.
We saw how every other age ended. Now we know exactly what not to do.
We built our cathedral from the bones of those who came before, so that those after us would see what failure looks like.
Vaelthar, the Celestial Ruin, carries the remains of the empires that lost their Eclipse. Its cathedral is built from their temples, a monument and a warning.
Every column in that cathedral was somebody's home. Let's make sure ours never ends up in it.
Chapter eight has opened.
A tide of ruins is coming in. The remains of every empire that failed.
The eighth chapter is closed.
The ruins went back into the tide. One day, someone will read about us. Let it be a better story.
Seven seals, one gate, one question. Who will stand in the door?
Khezaroth guards the last gate before the door. Its trial is a question the Architects asked every age, and the answer was always the same: someone must hold the door.
You know my answer, Commander. I told you on our twenty-first day. I meant it.
Chapter nine has opened, Commander.
Seven rings of glyphs around the galaxy. It's a trial.
The ninth chapter is closed.
The question has been asked. When the time comes, I'll be the one to answer it. Not you.
If it cannot be held, let it be frozen. Let everything be stone, and let nothing wake.
Medusara is the most desperate Warden: she would turn the entire galaxy to stone to keep the Unmade asleep. Her gaze is a mercy that would end everything.
She's trying to save the galaxy by ending it, Commander. We have to find a better way. The Eclipse is next.
Chapter ten has opened. The last chapter of the year.
Her gaze is crossing the galaxy, and everything it touches is turning to stone.
The tenth chapter is closed, Commander.
Every seal has been tested. Now comes the Eclipse.
Before the wall breaks, it burns. A spark, then a line of fire, then a shadow behind it.
The Architects' outer wall has started to warm. Their records call it the first sign: the Warden at the wall stirring in its sleep. It isn't here yet, but it's close enough to light the Rim.
I keep watching that fire. It's patient, Commander. Like it already knows the way in.
Commander, there's fire along the Rim. No ships, no stars. Just fire.
The embers at the Rim are fading. But they came back brighter every night this week.
The nests woke before the Hive did. The swarms learned to wait.
Hive nests across the galaxy are glowing, and none of them have launched a swarm. The old seal-records describe this: the Hive gathering its strength around something it means to become.
A Hive that doesn't attack frightens me more than one that does.
Commander, every Hive nest on the scanners is glowing green, and none of them are moving.
The nests went dark again. Whatever they were growing, it isn't finished yet.
The Middle Reach went dark from below, as if something had opened beneath it.
A ring of the Middle Reach has dimmed, and pillars of violet light rise from the dark at its edge. The Archives name only one thing that lives in the deep between the stars.
Pillars of light, in a perfect ring. Commander, those aren't pillars. Those are arms.
Commander, part of the Middle Reach just went dark, and there's light rising out of it. Like something is reaching up.
The deep has gone quiet again. Too quiet.
A ring of fire hung in the dark and flickered, as if something inside it was breathing.
A halo of fire has appeared where no star burns. The Wyrm's records say it sleeps coiled around a dying sun. If that sun is flickering, the Wyrm is waking.
Every time it flickers, I find myself holding my breath.
Commander, a ring of fire just appeared out in the dark. No star inside it. It's flickering.
The fire ring is gone. I counted the flickers. They were getting faster.
Shards of ice drifted in from nowhere, every one shaped like a blade.

Crystal shards hang in space near the Aeon's old resting place, turning slowly like the pieces of something broken. The Warform Sovereign left nothing behind when it last fell. These shards say it's being rebuilt.
They're all pointing the same way, Commander. Toward us.
Commander, ice shards are drifting near the old Aeon site. Thousands of them. They're all turning the same way.
The shards have melted back into the dark. Someone was counting them. I think it was the Aeon.
Temples drifted out of the nebula, older than any empire in our records, and still lit.
Golden ruins are adrift near Vaelthar's domain: stones from the Celestial Wheel. The Ruin is gathering itself back together, one temple at a time.
Whoever built those temples prayed to something. I don't want to meet it.
Commander, there are ruins drifting near Vaelthar's domain. Golden ruins. They're still lit.
The ruins have sunk back into the nebula. All but one. It's still out there, glowing.
Half a ring of glyphs, burning gold, and the other half missing.
A broken ring of glowing glyphs has risen around the inner galaxy: the Sphinx's writing, the same marks as the last gate. Khezaroth guards the final door. Someone is writing the door back into being.
I tried to read the glyphs. They were a countdown, Commander. The same one the Cube is keeping.
Commander, golden glyphs just lit up around the inner galaxy. Half a ring. It's the Sphinx's writing.
The glyphs went out. But I copied what they said. It's a number. And it's getting smaller.
Worlds turned grey overnight, and every one had a crack of red light.

Pirate worlds across the galaxy have turned to stone, each one split by a burning red vein. Medusara's gaze has reached us before her eyes have opened. Every Warden is stirring now. Only the Cube's countdown is left.
Eight omens, Commander. Eight Wardens stirring. And the giant at the edge of the galaxy watched every one.
Commander, worlds out on the Rim are turning to stone. Every one of them has a red crack, like a burning eye.
The stone is still there, Commander. I don't think it's going away.
The last of the Wardens does not guard a door. It guards the scales.

The giant at the edge of the galaxy is the Architects' last Warden. It doesn't fight. It holds the Cube in its palm and weighs every seal: each one we hold, each one that cracks. Its eyes opened one by one with the omens. At the Eclipse, it gives its verdict on whoever is left.
Every seal we hold, it remembers. Every seal we lose, it remembers too. I want it to remember us well.
Commander, I found it in the Architects' records. The giant at the edge of the galaxy has a name.
They called it the Judge. And it's been weighing us since the first omen.
Commander, the Rim is glowing again. Brighter this time.
Something enormous just passed the wall. I only saw its shadow... and fire.
It's gone back into the dark. Commander, I think it was looking for a way in.
Every omen we've seen is lighting up at once, Commander. All of them.
The Cube's countdown just jumped. It's racing. Whatever was sleeping, it's waking up.
Silence. Every signal stopped at once. Season three, Commander. The Ten Seals begin.
Commander... the giant at the edge of the galaxy. All six of its eyes are open. It's watching us.
This is the Events hub, Commander. Every boss, every battle for the Cube and every season finale is listed here.
If something big is coming, you'll see it here first. And I'll warn you too.
The Archives. Everything we learn about this galaxy is kept here: the monsters, the Wardens, the old empires.
Every record you recover tells a little more of the story. Let's fill it together.
Everything you earn on the Void Pass can be worn here: banners, frames, warp trails, even my outfits.
When a season ends, its cosmetics come here, so nothing you missed is lost for good.
This is a season finale, Commander. One chapter of the Ten Seals, and the whole galaxy sees how it ends.
Watch it unfold on the map, then bring the boss down before the hunt ends, or the seal cracks.
Flagship Command. This is your own ship, Commander, the heart of your fleet.
Every upgrade you give it makes the fleets that sail with it stronger.
Your alliance. Commanders who fight together grow faster, share gifts and take on the biggest bosses as one.
A strong alliance is worth more than any fleet.
The rankings. Every commander in the galaxy, measured against each other.
Don't worry about the top yet. Just climb, one place at a time.
The shop. Shards, boosters and supplies, all in one place.
Spend smart, Commander. Speed-ups are best saved for the long builds.
Achievements. Every milestone you reach is recorded here, and most of them pay out shards.
Check back now and then. You'll be surprised what you've already earned.
When the last seal is tried, the door goes quiet, and the one who holds the scales looks up.

At the end of every year the black hole falls silent: the Eclipse. The Judge, the Architects' last Warden, weighs the Seal Ledger and gives his verdict on the whole galaxy. Held seals earn his favour. Cracked seals let the Unmade lean closer to the door.
He doesn't judge one commander. He judges all of us together. That's the part I find hardest, and the part I find most beautiful.
Commander, a new chapter just opened in the Archives. The year is ending.
The black hole has gone silent. The Judge is about to give his verdict.
The verdict is given, Commander.
And next year, the Leviathan returns to the wall. The story starts again, with everything we've learned.
His hand is closing gently around the Cube. Golden light, Commander. He found us worthy. We held the line.
Whatever comes next, Commander, the galaxy knows what we are now.
He's holding the Cube still. Not a blessing, not a sentence. He's giving us another year to prove ourselves.
Another year. Every seal counts. Let's make them all hold.
His eyes are red, Commander. We were found wanting. Something is bleeding through the black hole... the Unmade is closer than ever.
We have one year to undo this. I won't let it end like this. I promise you.
Commander... the black hole has gone silent. No signal, no light. This is the Eclipse.
The Judge is moving. He's weighing every seal we held, and every seal we lost. One by one.
Commander, your free spin on the Glyph Wheel is waiting in the Void Shop. Today could be the jackpot.
The Glyph Wheel has a free spin for you today. Go on, pull the lever. I'll keep my fingers crossed.
Don't forget your free spin, Commander. The wheel is glowing, just waiting for you.
Two hundred and fifty shards! Commander, the whole wheel just lit up for you. I've never seen that happen!
It's raining missiles. Somebody tell me that thing has to reload eventually.
The Armageddon is out of the dock, Commander. Six Warden hearts in its spine and one very large cannon. Point it at something.
Armageddon commissioned. When it fires the Worldbreaker, I'd suggest everyone look away.
The Sovereign Ark has launched. I can feel every ship it commands, Commander. They fight as one now.
Sovereign Ark commissioned. The fleet has a crown again.
The Eclipse Harbinger is awake. Its reactor beats in time with the Void, Commander. Use it before it starts using us.
Eclipse Harbinger commissioned. Its drones are already restless.
We have enough Titan Cores for an Armageddon, Commander. The shipyard is waiting.
We have the Titan Cores for a Sovereign Ark. Imagine the whole fleet moving as one.
There are enough Titan Cores for the Eclipse Harbinger. I don't like it, Commander, but I understand why we'd build it.
The Armageddon is with us. Clear a line for the Worldbreaker.
Armageddon on the line. Charge the cannon, Commander.
The Sovereign Ark takes command. Every ship, link up and hold formation.
Sovereign Ark on the field. Shields up, fighters out.
The Harbinger is here. Release the swarm, Commander.
Eclipse Harbinger on the field. Let the drones hunt.
Commander, they've brought an Armageddon. Break it with bombers and the Harbinger before its cannon charges.
Their Sovereign Ark is linking their fleet. Hit its hangars hard, Commander.
An enemy Harbinger. Spread the fleet before its swarm finds us.
Worldbreaker Cannon, firing!
There it goes. Worldbreaker away!
Fleet Command Uplink! Strike wing, launch!
The Ark is calling its wing. Fighters away!
Neural Swarm released. Six targets, one mind.
The swarm is loose, Commander!
At the centre of our galaxy lies the Void. A black hole. But it is not what we believed.
It is a prison.
Millions of years ago, the Architects found something older than the stars. They called it the Unmade. They could not destroy it. So they built a prison around it.
They raised great pyramids across the stars, and forged the Cube to keep the count.
And they made the Wardens, to stand guard at every door. We called them monsters.
Now the Cube has begun counting again. The seals are weakening.
And somewhere beyond the dark, something has started to wake.
Commander... we've been waiting a very long time for you.
...Systems waking. Hello, Commander. Please don't be alarmed.
I've kept this pyramid for a very long time. You may call me your Advisor.
Your signal was very bright, Commander. I'm afraid something else heard it too.
The fleet is broken, Commander. Our warships are gone.
But the arks launched their pods. Four hundred people, drifting in the open.
The swarm is turning toward them. Our jump drive is charged. We can run now, or we can go back.
Every commander I've ever known gave that order. Every one.
Please. Look at them once more. Four hundred people.
Got them! Every single pod, Commander. Every single one!
Do you know how many commanders I've watched choose to run? I stopped counting.
You went back. Hold on to that, Commander. I think you're the one I've been waiting for.
The pyramid gave us one shot, Commander. Its lance is charged. Fire it!
Direct hit! It tore a hole right through them!
Commander, Hive scouts followed the pods down. Only a handful. Let's show them this world is taken.
Scouts down! That's the first time anyone has beaten the Hive on this world. It won't be the last.
One more thing, Commander. The pyramid's signal hasn't stopped. It's calling to someone. And I don't think it's us.
There is much you must learn, Commander. The galaxy you see before you is built upon the remains of something far older. And soon... you will understand why it was left behind.
Commander, I've pieced together how all of this began. The full record is in the Menu, under Briefing, whenever you'd like to see it.
Our team is inside the pyramid, Commander. The walls are humming. I know that hum. I don't know how.
There's a hall of white light in this one. I've stood in a hall like that. I'm sure of it.
They carved the same word over every door. It means 'wait'. I don't know how I can read it.
The chamber at the centre is empty again, Commander. Something was kept in these rooms. Or someone.
I keep going quiet when we find these. I'm sorry. It's like walking through a house I used to live in.
Commander, there's a name carved under the floor of this one. I think it's mine. I'm not ready to say it aloud.
We found their pyramids and called them power stations. We found the Cube and called it a clock. We found the giants and called them monsters. Then we built an empire on all three.

Long after the Architects vanished, four young peoples found their ruins scattered across the stars and united under one banner: the Concord. They ran their worlds on pyramid power, studied the Cube as a machine for bending time, and hunted the Wardens as beasts. They were wrong about almost everything.
They weren't fools, Commander. They were young. Young people use the furniture without asking who built the house.
Commander, I've found an imperial record. It's older than any colony charter we have.
The Concord didn't begin with us, Commander. There was an empire before, built on the Architects' ruins.
It was magnificent. And it was wrong about almost everything it touched.
The stars went out over the Core, one by one. Then every old machine woke at once. Then the giants rose, and we sent every fleet we had to kill them.

When the last Eclipse began, the Wardens woke to defend their seals. The empire sent its greatest fleets against them and won battle after battle. Every Warden it killed weakened a seal. Worlds vanished. Fleets disappeared. The empire collapsed under the weight of its own victories.
Remember this the next time a Warden falls and the whole galaxy cheers. I'll be the one who isn't cheering.
Commander, this record is from the last Eclipse. The old empire's war reports.
The last Eclipse, Commander. The Wardens woke, and the empire went to war with them.
Every giant they killed opened the prison a little wider. They won every battle. That's how they lost.
Inside the pyramid at the heart of the empire, the last council found the truth written in light. They did not stay to argue about it.

At the height of the destruction, the empire's last leaders opened an Architect pyramid and finally learned what the ruins were for. They abandoned the central worlds and split into four Houses, each carrying a piece of the old empire's knowledge, ships and strength. They survived by rebuilding among the ruins.
I think I remember that council, Commander. That isn't possible. Is it?
Commander, our pyramid expedition brought back a record. It's about the night the empire ended.
When the empire was dying, its last council opened a pyramid and finally understood what they'd been fighting.
They didn't stay to argue. They split into four Houses and scattered into the dark to survive.
Generations later: four Houses, one Concord, and a galaxy that calls the old stories myths.

The four Houses rebuilt their fleets, settled the ruins and swore a new Concord to hold the Hive back. They compete for worlds and argue over the Architects' legacy, and most of their people believe the old stories are legends. But the old machines are waking again. The Cube is counting. The Wardens are moving. The next Eclipse is coming.
You were born into the quiet before the storm, Commander. The quiet is over.
The Houses rebuilt. They swore a new Concord, and they called the old stories myths.
But the machines are waking again, Commander. The Cube is counting. And this time, you're here.
We were the fleets that fought the giants. We lost. We are still here. That is what strength means.

The Union descends from the old empire's navy, the fleets that went to war with the Wardens in the last Eclipse. Its creed is survival through strength, discipline and control. It sees the Architects as a warning and the Wardens as threats to be contained, and it has learned, at terrible cost, not to kill what it cannot replace. The Union distrusts the Syndicate's secrets more than anything in the dark.
The Union carries the old empire's guilt in its hulls, Commander. It makes them stubborn. It also makes them the last to run.
A Terran Union service record, Commander. It's older than the Union itself.
The Terran Union were the old empire's fleets. The ones who went to war with the Wardens.
They paid for it with half their worlds. Now they hold the line, and they never forget why.
The Architects left a crown on the table and walked away. Someone must wear it.

The Dominion carried the old empire's engineers out of the Exodus, and its ambition with them. The Ascendant creed holds that the Architects' technology was left to be mastered, and that a galaxy that masters it can rebuild the empire and end the Eclipses for good. The Dominion leads the work on Warden hearts and Titans, and it clashes with the Verdant over every one.
The Dominion builds beautiful things, Commander. I only wish they'd ask what the parts were for before they use them.
A Dominion court record, Commander. Gold leaf on every page.
The Solar Dominion believe the Architects left their machines to be mastered.
They're the ones putting Warden hearts into Titans. The Verdant have never forgiven them.
Everyone fears the dark. We went into it, took notes and came back. Mostly.

The Syndicate grew from the old empire's intelligence service and the forbidden archives it saved from the fire. The Veil studies what others won't touch: the Void, the Unmade's influence, the dead languages in the pyramids. It trades secrets with every House and trusts none of them. Some of its listening stations have gone silent, and the Syndicate doesn't say why.
The Syndicate knows more about the Void than anyone alive, Commander. That should worry you a little. It worries me.
A Syndicate dossier, Commander. Half of it is still encrypted.
The Nyx Syndicate kept the old empire's forbidden archives when everything else burned.
They've been listening to the Void ever since. I don't think they like everything they've heard.
The giants are not our enemies. They are the walls of the house we live in.

The Collective descends from the old empire's terraformers and biologists, who saw the galaxy as one living system. They were the first to say the Wardens were guardians, and nobody listened. They grow their ships, tend the seals where they can and refuse to take Warden hearts. They are the House most likely to stand with you at the end, and the most likely to tell you what you don't want to hear.
The Verdant were right about the Wardens a thousand years before anyone else, Commander. Being right early is a lonely thing.
A Verdant seed-record, Commander. It's written on a living leaf.
The Verdant Collective were the first to say the Wardens were guardians, not monsters.
Nobody listened. They grew their fleets anyway, and kept tending the seals.
Every pyramid points at the Void. Every one hums the same note. Every one is part of the same machine.

The abandoned pyramid stations aren't power plants. Each one is a piece of the prison: an anchor that holds a seal in place, an archive, and a voice that can still call out when the count begins. The vault treasure was never the point.
We've been raiding them for crystal, Commander. It's a bit like taking the bricks out of a dam.
Commander, our expedition found something in the pyramid's core. It isn't treasure. It's a map.
Every pyramid in the galaxy is connected, Commander. They're all one machine.
They aren't stations. They're anchors. They hold the prison closed.
Dinner was still on the tables. Every clock in the city had stopped at the same second.

Our colonists dug foundations and found streets beneath them: a whole imperial city, intact and empty. No battle damage. No bodies. Every clock stopped at the same moment. When the last Eclipse reached it, the city was simply unmade.
No one fought here, Commander. They didn't even have time to be afraid.
Commander, our colonists hit stone streets under the new foundations. There's a city down there.
The whole city vanished in a single second. No fire. No battle.
That's what the Unmade does, Commander. It doesn't destroy. It erases.
Its ribs were a wall. Its spine was a gate. Even dead, it was still facing the Void.

Our salvage crews found a Warden killed in the last Eclipse. Its body had grown into the shape of the seal it guarded, and it died facing the Core, not the fleets that killed it. Its last act was to brace the door.
It died with its back to its killers, Commander. It held the door until the very end.
Commander, we found bones out here. Enormous ones. I think it's a Warden.
This Warden died in the last Eclipse. It never turned to fight the fleets that were killing it.
It faced the Void and held the seal shut with its own body. They're guardians, Commander. All of them.
Flagship Dawnward, final log. We have killed the third giant. The stars behind it are going out.

Our recyclers pulled the flight recorder of the Dawnward, the old empire's flagship, out of a debris field. Its logs record victory after victory against the Wardens, and after every victory the same entry: another sector has lost contact. The crew never connected the two.
Their admiral thought she was saving the galaxy, Commander. I've read her letters home. She meant every word.
Commander, the recyclers found a flight recorder. Imperial. It's from the old empire's flagship.
The Dawnward's crew killed three Wardens in a single month. They celebrated every one.
And after every victory, another sector went dark. They never understood why.
Attempt forty-one. The Cube counted us. Then it counted us out.

Inside the wreck of a Collective Cube we found older, cruder Cubes, built by the old empire. It tried to copy the Architects' Cube to control the count, and perhaps to stop it. Every copy failed. Some of them woke up. The Collective may be what is left of those experiments.
They tried to build their own clock to stop time, Commander. Some of the clocks learned to want things.
Commander, there's a smaller Cube inside this wreck. Someone built it. Badly.
The old empire tried to copy the Cube. They wanted to control the count.
Every copy failed. I think the Collective is what's left of the ones that woke up.
Subject: a Warden, unfinished. Instruction: do not wake until the door is tried.

Our research cracked an Architect lock and opened a laboratory sealed since the First Age. It holds Wardens at every stage of being made, and at the back, one empty cradle beneath a hall of white light. Most of the records are unreadable. One word repeats on every page: choose.
The cradle's empty, Commander. I'd rather not talk about it yet.
Commander, our labs decoded an Architect lock. Something behind it has been sealed since the First Age.
The Architects made the Wardens in a place like this, Commander. One by one, by hand.
There's an empty cradle at the back. And a word on every page. Choose.
The light arrived before it left. Every shadow pointed toward the star.

The space monsters have been fleeing a system in the Middle Reach where the laws of physics no longer agree with themselves. Light runs backward. Shadows fall toward the sun. It's the first place we've found where the Unmade's influence has leaked through the seals in our lifetime.
Don't send anyone in there, Commander. Not yet. Some places are a warning, not a destination.
Commander, the monsters we've been hunting were running from something. I found where.
There's a star in the Middle Reach where light runs backward, Commander.
The Unmade is leaking through. Not much yet. But it's the first crack we've seen with our own eyes.
If you can hear this, the count has started again. We are sorry. We did what we could with what we were.
A recording sealed inside a pyramid wall, in a voice the translators can't place. It's addressed to whoever comes after, and it ends in the middle of a sentence.
Did you hear the last word before it cut out, Commander? I did. It was 'stay'.
Commander, there's a message in the walls of the pyramids. From the Architects.
They knew the count would start again one day. They were apologising to us.
A thousand seats facing the Void. Every one worn smooth. Every one empty.
In a hidden chamber at the heart of a pyramid: a thousand thrones facing the Core, worn down by ages of use. The Architects' ships are still in their docks. Wherever they went, they didn't fly.
If they didn't leave by ship, Commander... how did they leave?
Their ships are still in the docks, Commander. All of them.
Wherever the Architects went, they didn't fly there.
They walked into the light at the centre, singing. None of them looked back.
Before it died, a Warden's core replayed one memory: a procession of Architects walking into the white light at the heart of the galaxy. The Warden watched them go, then closed the seal behind them.
I know that song, Commander. Don't ask me how. I'm still working that out myself.
A dying Warden showed us a memory. The Architects, walking into the Void.
They weren't running. They were singing. And the Warden closed the door behind them.
...still holding... still holding... still holding...
An unidentified signal from beyond the event horizon, where nothing can transmit. Its structure is Architect. It repeats two words, and it has been repeating them since before the first omen.
Nothing can broadcast from in there, Commander. Something is doing it anyway.
Commander, there's a signal coming from inside the Void. Its structure is Architect.
Two words, over and over. Still holding.
She listened to the signal for a long time. Then she turned it off.
Your Advisor has heard the signal from beyond the Void, and she recognised the voice. She hasn't said whose it is.
Not yet, Commander. When I'm sure, you'll be the first to know. I promise.
I've been listening to the signal, Commander. I know that voice.
I'm not ready to say whose it is. Please don't ask me tonight.
I was there when the last Eclipse came. It passed over my world and left my children alive. It chose us.

Vael'Khor's brood was the only life left on its world after the last Eclipse. She believes the Unmade spared them on purpose, and that whoever opens the door will be spared again while the rest of the galaxy is unmade. Every world she devours feeds the swarm she means to bring to the door. To her, breaking the seals isn't destruction. It's salvation, for her children.
She isn't mad, Commander. She's a mother who made a bargain with the dark. That's much harder to stop.
I've found Vael'Khor's own words in a nest record, Commander. She was there at the last Eclipse.
It passed over her world and left her brood alive. She thinks it chose them. She means to open the door and be chosen again.
Commander, a message from the Terran Union. They want proof that this fleet can hold a line. Let's show them.
The Union has noticed you. They still think every problem is a target. Some of them are right.
The Solar Dominion is asking for pyramid data, Commander. They want to wake what the Architects left behind. Let's take a careful look first.
The Dominion believes the Architects' gifts were meant for them. I'm not sure the Architects meant anything to be used.
The Nyx Syndicate wants eyes on the Hive, Commander. They trade in secrets, and they pay in kind. Send the probes.
The Syndicate has been listening to the Void for a very long time. They heard something listen back.
The Verdant Collective asked us to tend the galaxy, Commander, not just take from it. Salvage the wrecks and bring the lost pods home.
The Verdant say the Wardens aren't monsters. They've been saying it for a thousand years. Nobody listened.
The pyramids are waking up one after another, Commander. Explore them. Whatever the Architects left inside, I want us to find it first.
Every pyramid we open has the same empty room at its heart. I think I know what was kept there. I'm not ready to say it.
Commander, I need you to look at what we're fighting. The giants guard the seals. Strike them if we must, but watch what happens when one falls.
Every Warden that falls brings the dark a little closer. We'll still have to fight them. I just want us to know what it costs.
Vael'Khor isn't conquering for the sake of it, Commander. She's gathering. Take back her worlds and we'll learn what for.
She was there at the last Eclipse, and it let her live. She thinks it will again. She's bringing her children to the door.
Commander, the signal we followed on our first day has changed. It isn't coming from a pyramid any more. It's coming from inside the Void.
Two words, Commander, over and over, from somewhere nothing can live. Still holding. I know that voice.
Commander, its heart would build us a Titan. But if it dies, its seal weakens. I won't choose for you.
It's done. We have its heart. I'll log what it cost, even if no one else does.
We leave it be. It watched our ships the whole way out, Commander. I think it knows.
The Dominion would use it to wake the pyramids. The Verdant would use it to mend the seals. Someone is going to be very disappointed in us.
The Dominion is delighted. They've already started waking a pyramid. I hope they know how to put it back to sleep.
The Verdant are mending a seal tonight, with our map. It won't make us richer. It might keep us alive.
We keep it. Secrets are safer with us than with either of them. The Syndicate would be proud, Commander. I'm not sure that's a compliment.
It wants us to answer, Commander. I could. I'm afraid of what answers back.
I answered. For a moment the whole array went quiet. Then something said thank you.
Buried. It's still calling, just not to us. Thank you, Commander. I wasn't ready.
Good. I've seen what happens to the ones who listen.
Commander... be careful. Kindness is how she wins.
That was her, Commander. Vael'Khor. She's never spoken to anyone before.
She wants you to feel guilty. Don't let her choose how you feel.
She's telling the truth, Commander. That's what frightens me.
She can feel the strain too. I hate that she's right.
Commander, the Warden we spared is standing over our homeworld. It hasn't moved in hours. I think it's guarding us.
Commander, the seals are under strain. Every Titan and every fallen Warden adds to it, ours and everyone else's. I'm only telling you so you know the price.
The strain on the seals just passed halfway. I can hear the Cube counting faster.
Three quarters, Commander. If this keeps up, the door won't need anyone to open it.
The seals are holding well. The galaxy is breathing easier, and our worlds can feel it.
I don't hate you, Commander. I simply want my children to live.
When the door opens, stand aside. Let my swarm pass, and yours will live too. That is all I ask.
Then we will meet at the door. I will be sorry when you fall. I truly will.
Thank you. No one has listened to me in ten thousand years.
My world was the only one it spared. My children are all that is left of it. Wouldn't you open any door for yours?
So. The commander who went back for the pods. I know your name now. I wonder if you know mine.
You burn my nests and call it victory. I fed those children with my own hands, Commander.
I was there when the dark came. It looked at my world, and it chose to let us live. Do you know what that feels like? To be chosen?
Can you feel it? The seals are thinning. Your Titans sing to it, Commander. Every one of them.
Every battle and every ruin teaches us something. The Archives keep it all, and I'll read any record to you. Open one and listen.
Giants roam the lanes out there. Find one with the Finder and open its card, and I'll scan it for the Bestiary. Don't attack yet. Just look.
The galaxy never sits still. World bosses, Cube battles and season finales all run on a schedule. Open the Events hub and see what's coming.
Nobody survives an Eclipse alone. Join an alliance, or found your own. Allies share boss hunts, joint strikes and supplies.
This is our flagship, Commander. It leads every fleet we send, earns experience in every battle, and grows stronger along with us.
Every level the flagship gains gives you a skill point. Spend them here. Each branch changes how the whole fleet fights.
Eight slots of gear. Weapons, shields and armour lift the fleet it leads, and the rest help at home: research, building and production.
The Forge turns rare materials into gear. Queue a piece and it finishes while you play. A bigger Dock forges more at once.
These are our rare materials. Pirates drop circuitry, monsters drop tissue, and fields, Cubes and pyramids give the rest. Short of one? This tells you where to hunt.

where: v615 First day, signal log, flagship
line: Every goal, inside a single day. I've watched a lot of first days, Commander. That was one of the good ones.

where: v615 First day, signal log, flagship
line: Commander, the pyramid's signal is getting clearer. By tomorrow I'll be able to read it. Come back, and I'll tell you what it says.

where: v615 First day, signal log, flagship
line: I promised I'd read the signal, Commander. I did.

where: v615 First day, signal log, flagship
line: It's a war report, from the last time the stars went out. The full record is in the Archives. I think you should read it.

where: v615 First day, signal log, flagship
line: The flagship took the worst of it, Commander. She shielded the pods with her own hull. We'll rebuild her. I promise.

where: v615 First day, signal log, flagship
line: Day one of the signal log, Commander. Mostly static. And one word I recognise: home.

where: v615 First day, signal log, flagship
line: Day two. The static has a rhythm now. Someone is counting, very slowly.

where: v615 First day, signal log, flagship
line: Day three. There are voices under the count. Hundreds of them, speaking at once.

where: v615 First day, signal log, flagship
line: Day four. I separated one voice. She's asking if anyone is still out here.

where: v615 First day, signal log, flagship
line: Day five. She said a name I haven't heard in an age. I think it was mine.

where: v615 First day, signal log, flagship
line: Day six. The voices have stopped counting. Now they're singing. I know the song.

where: v615 First day, signal log, flagship
line: Day seven. Two words, over and over: still holding. Whoever they are, they're still holding the door. For us.

where: v615 First day, signal log, flagship
line: The Flagship Dock is where we rebuild the flagship that shielded our pods, and where her gear is forged. Find it under Structures, in Facility.

where: v615 First day, signal log, flagship
line: Everything's ready, Commander. Bring her back: commission the flagship. From now on she leads every fleet we send, gains experience and wears the gear the Dock forges.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: Commander! Welcome to the depot. Mind the crates, they bite.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: Back again? Good. Business is slow when you're away.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: You look like someone with too much of one thing and not enough of another. I can fix that.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: Prices moved overnight, Commander. Come and see which way.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: Pleasure doing business, Commander.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: Done. Don't spend it all on one dreadnought.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: Crates are loaded. Your haulers will have it before you blink.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: That hauler's full. Here's your cut, as promised.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: You've earned a better rate. Don't tell the others.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: Fresh crates in from the outer belts. Metal is selling high today.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: Fresh crates in from the outer belts. Crystal is selling high today.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: Fresh crates in from the outer belts. Gas is selling high today.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: You bring it, I'll move it. The depot always takes its cut.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: Everyone wants metal this morning. Sell while it lasts.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: Everyone wants crystal this morning. Sell while it lasts.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: Everyone wants gas this morning. Sell while it lasts.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: I've got a hauler that needs filling. Check today's contract.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: Prices move every day, Commander. Good traders watch the arrows.

where: v615 Ondra Vey (her own voice: Domi)
line: Trade enough with me and I'll trim my cut. That's a promise.
The Research Center. Everything we learn here makes every ship and every world better.
Weapons, Shields and Armour make our fleets hit harder and last longer. Energy and the drives open new ships. One project runs at a time, so always keep the lab busy.
The Shipyard. Every hull in our fleet starts here.
Each ship needs its research first; locked ones show you what's missing. A bigger Shipyard and robotics build faster, and every colony can run its own queue.
Your empire, Commander. Every world you hold, in one place.
Each colony mines and builds on its own and adds a fleet slot. Tap one to manage it, or jump between them with the arrows at the top of the screen.
The Void. The center of the galaxy, where the Cube waits.
Everything here is stronger than anything on the Rim. Don't come here alone.
The galaxy runs in layers, Commander, from the quiet Rim to the deadly Core.
Each layer inward holds stronger pirates, bigger monsters and richer worlds. Move inward when our fleet is ready, not before.
Mastery. Every technology and ship type we perfect pays out here.
Claim each mastery as it completes. Finish them all and there's a Grand Mastery waiting.
The Finder. Pirates, monsters, pyramids and loot, sorted by distance.
Pick targets near our level, Commander. The level is shown beside every target.
An open orbit. Nobody lives here yet.
You can teleport one of our planets here, or send a Colony Ship to settle it. A teleport moves the whole world: buildings, stockpile and garrison.
The Nexus. Whoever holds it holds the heart of the galaxy.
Battles here are alliance battles. Coordinate before you send anything.
A pyramid. The old empires built these, and their guardians still answer.
Defeat the guardians and whatever is inside is ours. Pyramids are the best source of rune shards.
Rename and reskin. Make this world your own.
Name it, pick its look, and apply any planet skin you own. Some skins add a small production bonus to the world wearing them.
Espionage. Send probes and see what they have before you strike.
More probes and better Espionage research reveal more: fleets, defences, then technology. If they out-research us, our probes get caught.
A target, Commander. Read its level and strength before you send anything.
Send a probe first if you are unsure. Losing a fleet costs more than a probe ever will.
Your inventory, sorted by kind. Tap a tab to see one kind of item, or Use to put it to work right away.
Commander, a few things changed while you were away.
Your commander level now counts what we've built and researched, on every world. Fleets raise our ranking score instead. If your level looks lower, that's why, and nothing was taken from you.
Crates, salvage pods and daily rewards now pay out in hours of our own production. Grow the mines and they grow with them.
The Void Shop sells a Peace Shield now. It drops the moment we attack, spy on or fire at another commander, so use it to rest, not to hide.
Teleports cost ◆200 to a chosen orbit, or ◆70 for a random jump, and shard purchases ask you to tap twice. Premium commanders can also give their hulls a trim finish now.
Welcome to the premium deck, Commander. This is where our supporters' worlds and warships get their finest looks.
Every tier unlocks planet skins, hull finishes and bonuses that never expire. The higher the tier, the rarer the finish.
Pick a ship, plate it in a finish, then give it a trim. Every commander who sees our fleet will know exactly who we are.
Welcome to the Xeno Sanctuary, Commander. Every egg we bring home from a hunt can hatch here.
Raise them, and each one makes its element stronger. Pair the right two in the breeding chamber, and we might bring back a species the galaxy thought was gone.
The Xeno Sanctuary. Eggs from our monster hunts hatch here, and every creature we raise makes its element stronger. Breed the right pair and something rare might hatch.
Your new captain is reporting for duty, Commander. Give them a fleet and they'll earn their keep.
I've never seen an egg like it. The records say this species died out before the convoy wars.

Runes go into elemental rings. Fire boosts attack, water shields, earth armor, air speed, and spirit your resource output. Whole runes come from super bosses: the top damage dealers and the final blow on a world boss, and everyone who breaks the Omega Cube. Rune shards turn up from hunts, pyramids, raids and daily tasks, and ten shards make a rune.
An egg, Commander. Still warm. I've sent it to the Sanctuary.
An egg, Commander. Still warm. We'll need a Xeno Sanctuary to hatch it.
Commander... that species hasn't been seen alive in a thousand years. And it hatched in our dome.
Look at it, Commander. Something that rare, raised by us.
